patterns.name: Container-Native AI Architecture as Industry Standard
patterns.description: GPT-class models and AI services are deployed using Docker containers by default in 2025. The integration is implicit rather than explicit - containers are the standard deployment mechanism for AI.
patterns.evidence: 95 GPT mentions (9.2%) + 40 Docker mentions (3.9%) across 1,029 learnings. GPT-5.1 release (513 HN score) shows advanced models requiring robust deployment infrastructure. No explicit 'gpt-docker' projects, indicating natural convergence.

strategies: Use Docker for all AI model deployments
Container orchestration (K8s, Cloud Run) for scaling
Resource allocation (CPU, memory, GPU) in container specs

applicability_to_chained.justification: Chained already implements container-native AI architecture. ADK agents, Error Observer, and other AI services deployed in Docker on Cloud Run. This pattern validates existing approach.

actionable_next_steps: Continue using Docker + Cloud Run for AI agents
Create templates for new AI services (optional)
Monitor GPT evolution for resource impacts (passive)

patterns.name: Local Development to Production Deployment Tooling Gap
patterns.description: Developers use docker-compose for local AI development but lack seamless tools to translate to production (AWS Copilot, Cloud Run, K8s). Manual translation is required.
patterns.evidence: AWS Copilot CLI Issue #1612: Request for docker-compose import feature. Community states 'Docker compose is commonly used for local development and testing' but production deployment requires manual manifest creation.

strategies: Standardize docker-compose files for AI services
Use infrastructure-as-code for both local and prod
tools: gcloud CLI for Cloud Run deployment

applicability_to_chained.justification: Low priority developer experience improvement. Chained's current deployment process (Terraform + gcloud) works well. Standardized templates could speed up new agent development but not urgent.
applicability_to_chained.implementation: VERY LOW complexity - 2-4 hours for templates

actionable_next_steps: Optional: Create docker-compose templates in infrastructure/docker/templates/
Optional: Document docker-compose → Cloud Run translation
No urgent action required - current process is sufficient

patterns.name: Next-Generation LLM Deployment Infrastructure Requirements
patterns.description: GPT-5.1 and future advanced models require production-grade deployment infrastructure with scalability, resource management, and monitoring. Container orchestration is essential.
patterns.evidence: GPT-5.1 announcement (513 HN score) - 'A smarter, more conversational ChatGPT'. Advanced conversational AI requires robust infrastructure for production deployment at scale.

strategies: Version control and A/B testing for models
tools: GCP Artifact Registry for model storage

applicability_to_chained.justification: Chained's Cloud Run + Docker architecture already supports these requirements. Future-proofed for advanced models. May need to adjust resource allocations as models evolve.
applicability_to_chained.implementation: Already in place - monitor for changes
applicability_to_chained.impact: LOW - strategic awareness, no immediate action

actionable_next_steps: Monitor GPT-5.x and advanced model releases
Adjust Cloud Run memory/CPU allocations if needed

decisions_validated.decision: Use Docker containers for all AI agents (ADK, Error Observer, etc.)
decisions_validated.evidence: Industry standard in 2025. 95 GPT mentions + 40 Docker mentions show natural convergence. GPT-5.1 requiring robust infrastructure validates container approach.
decisions_validated.impact: Chained's architecture aligns with industry best practices. No changes needed.

decisions_validated.decision: Deploy AI agents to GCP Cloud Run (vs self-managed Kubernetes)
decisions_validated.evidence: Container orchestration is essential for AI deployment. Cloud Run provides managed scaling, networking, and monitoring without K8s operational complexity.
decisions_validated.impact: Correct choice for Chained's scale and team size. Avoids operational burden while maintaining scalability.

decisions_validated.decision: Use Python for AI agent implementation
decisions_validated.evidence: Python is de-facto standard for AI/ML (transformers, torch, FastAPI). All 95 GPT-related learnings implicitly assume Python ecosystem.
decisions_validated.impact: Chained's Python-based agents align with industry. Access to rich ecosystem of AI libraries.

anti_patterns_identified.anti_pattern: Building custom deployment tools instead of using industry standards
anti_patterns_identified.example: Avoiding Docker and creating custom deployment mechanisms
anti_patterns_identified.why_problematic: Reinventing the wheel. Docker is proven, portable, and has vast ecosystem. Custom tools increase maintenance burden.
anti_patterns_identified.remedy: Use Docker + orchestration (Cloud Run, K8s). Focus on agent logic, not infrastructure tooling.

anti_patterns_identified.example: Running models directly on VMs without Docker
anti_patterns_identified.why_problematic: Inconsistent environments, dependency conflicts, difficult scaling, hard to reproduce. Non-portable across clouds.
anti_patterns_identified.remedy: Containerize all AI services with Docker. Use Cloud Run or K8s for orchestration.

anti_patterns_identified.example: Tribal knowledge for deploying new AI agents
anti_patterns_identified.why_problematic: Slows down new agent development. Hard for new developers to contribute. Patterns not reusable.
anti_patterns_identified.remedy: Document AI container architecture, create templates, write deployment guides.

priority_low.recommendation: Create docker-compose templates for AI agents

world_model_impact.strategic_positioning: Chained's architecture validated by industry trends. Container-native AI is standard approach. No urgent changes needed.
